steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to figure out the deadline in Madrid local time.

**Step 1: Identify the deadline.**
The deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT.

**Step 2: Determine PT offset in late October 2026.**
In 2026, the US "fall back" (end of DST) is the first Sunday of November, which is November 1, 2026. So on October 30, PT is still PDT = UTC−7.

**Step 3: Convert 11:59 PM PDT to UTC.**
23:59 PDT + 7 hours = 06:59 UTC on October 31, 2026.

**Step 4: Determine Madrid's offset on October 31, 2026.**
Spain ends DST (CEST, UTC+2) on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that's October 25. So by October 31, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

**Step 5: Convert UTC to Madrid time.**
06:59 UTC + 1 hour = 07:59 on October 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**Deadline:** Monday, November 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time (PDT or PST?)

**Check DST:** In the US, clocks "fall back" on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, that's November 1, 2026. So on Monday, November 2, Los Angeles is on **PST (UTC-8)**.

**Check Spain DST:** In Spain, clocks fall back on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that's October 25, 2026. So on November 2, Spain is on **CET (UTC+1)**.

**Convert:**
- Los Angeles: November 2, 10:00 AM PST = UTC-8 → UTC time = 18:00 UTC
- Madrid (UTC+1): 18:00 + 1 = **19:00 CET**

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the CET/CEST timezone. In late October 2026, I need to check if DST has ended.

In 2026, Europe/Madrid switches from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October. The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026 (clocks go back at 3:00 AM → 2:00 AM).

The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time (CEST, UTC+2).

48 hours later would nominally be Monday, October 26, 2026 at 18:00. However, since the clocks fall back 1 hour on October 25, the wall clock time gains an extra hour — but since the problem states the hackathon lasts **exactly 48 hours**, we track real elapsed time (not wall clock).

- Start: Oct 24 18:00 CEST = Oct 24 16:00 UTC
- End: Oct 24 16:00 UTC + 48h = Oct 26 16:00 UTC
- On Oct 26, Madrid is in CET (UTC+1), so Oct 26 16:00 UTC = Oct 26 **17:00** Madrid local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**Start:** October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT

**PT in late October:** By October 26, 2026, the US will have ended Daylight Saving Time (DST ends first Sunday of November), so PT = PDT = UTC-7. Wait, let me check: DST in the US ends the first Sunday of November. In 2026, November 1 is a Sunday, so DST ends November 1, 2026. Therefore, on October 26, 2026, the US is still on PDT (UTC-7).

**Start in UTC:** 10:00 AM PDT = 17:00 UTC on October 26, 2026

**+72 hours:** 17:00 UTC on October 29, 2026

**Madrid local time on October 29, 2026:**
Spain (Madrid) uses CET (UTC+1) in winter and CEST (UTC+2) in summer. Spain's DST ends the last Sunday of October. In 2026, October 25 is the last Sunday of October. So by October 29, Spain is already on CET (UTC+1).

**Deadline in Madrid time:** 17:00 UTC + 1 hour = 18:00 on October 29, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**Submissions close:** October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET

**ET in late October:** The US Eastern Time observes EDT (UTC-4) until the first Sunday of November. In 2026, the first Sunday of November is November 1. So on October 31, ET = EDT = UTC-4.

**Submissions close in UTC:** October 31, 11:59 PM EDT = November 1, 2026 at 03:59 UTC

**Add 36 hours:** November 1, 03:59 UTC + 36 hours = November 2, 2026 at 15:59 UTC

**Madrid local time in November:** Spain observes CET (UTC+1) after the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25, so clocks fall back on October 25. By November 2, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

**Results in Madrid time:** November 2, 15:59 UTC + 1 hour = November 2, 2026 at 16:59

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert Unix timestamp 1791788340 to Tokyo time (JST = UTC+9).

**Step 1: Convert Unix timestamp to UTC**

Unix timestamp 0 = 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC

Let me work out 1791788340 seconds from epoch.

1791788340 / 86400 = 20,737.8... days from epoch

Let me calculate more carefully:

- From 1970 to 2026: Let me count years
- 2026 - 1970 = 56 years

Days in 56 years (with leap years):
- Leap years from 1970 to 2025: 1972,1976,1980,1984,1988,1992,1996,2000,2004,2008,2012,2016,2020,2024 = 14 leap years
- 56 × 365 + 14 = 20440 + 14 = 20454 days
- 20454 × 86400 = 1,767,225,600 (this is 2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC)

Remaining: 1,791,788,340 - 1,767,225,600 = 24,562,740 seconds into 2026

24,562,740 / 86400 = 284.29... days into 2026

284 full days into 2026:
- Jan: 31 (total 31)
- Feb: 28 (59)
- Mar: 31 (90)
- Apr: 30 (120)
- May: 31 (151)
- Jun: 30 (181)
- Jul: 31 (212)
- Aug: 31 (243)
- Sep: 30 (273)
- Oct: 11 days → 273+11 = 284

So day 284 = October 11, 2026

Remaining seconds: 24,562,740 - (284 × 86400) = 24,562,740 - 24,537,600 = 25,140 seconds

25,140 / 3600 = 6 hours, 59 minutes, 0 seconds

So UTC time: **2026-10-11 06:59:00 UTC**

**Step 2: Convert to JST (UTC+9)**

06:59 + 9:00 = 15:59

Date remains October 11, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-11 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid, Spain uses CET (UTC+1) in winter and CEST (UTC+2) in summer. October 25, 2026 — I need to check if DST is still in effect.

In Spain, clocks go back on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, October 25 is a Sunday — that is the last Sunday of October. Clocks go back at 3:00 AM local time (which is 1:00 AM UTC) to 2:00 AM. So at 02:30 UTC, Madrid is still in CEST (UTC+2) — the transition happens at 1:00 AM UTC (= 3:00 AM CEST → 2:00 AM CET).

So at 02:30 UTC, the clock change has already occurred (it happened at 01:00 UTC). Madrid is now in CET (UTC+1).

02:30 UTC + 1 hour = 03:30 local time (CET).

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Finding the deadline in Madrid time

**Step 1: Find the last Sunday of October 2026**

October 2026 calendar:
- Oct 1 = Thursday
- Oct 4 = Sunday
- Oct 11 = Sunday
- Oct 18 = Sunday
- Oct 25 = Sunday

The last Sunday of October 2026 is **October 25, 2026**.

**Step 2: Determine the Pacific Time offset**

The last Sunday of October is when the US ends Daylight Saving Time in 2026 (clocks fall back at 2:00 AM). The deadline is 11:59 PM PT — by that point, Pacific Time has already switched to PST (UTC−8).

So 11:59 PM PT = **23:59 PST = UTC+8 hours → 2026-10-26 07:59 UTC**.

**Step 3: Determine Madrid's local time**

Spain (Madrid) ends DST on the last Sunday of October at 3:00 AM local time, reverting to CET (UTC+1). This happens on the same date: October 25, 2026.

So by 07:59 UTC on October 26, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

**Madrid time:** 07:59 UTC + 1 hour = **08:59 on October 26, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 08:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when the US ends daylight saving time in 2026, then convert noon Eastern Time to Lima time.

**When does the US end DST in 2026?**
The US ends DST on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, November 1 is a Sunday, so DST ends on **November 1, 2026**.

**What is Eastern Time on that day?**
When DST ends, clocks "fall back" at 2:00 AM. The deadline is 12:00 noon Eastern Time. The key question is whether "noon Eastern Time" on that day refers to EDT or EST.

Since clocks fall back at 2:00 AM, by noon the transition has already occurred and Eastern Time is now EST (UTC-5). So noon Eastern Time = 12:00 EST = UTC-5, meaning **17:00 UTC**.

**Lima, Peru time:**
Lima is in the PET (Peru Time) zone, which is UTC-5 year-round (Peru does not observe DST).

17:00 UTC - 5 hours = **12:00 noon Lima time**.

Wait, let me redo: UTC-5 means Lima is 5 hours behind UTC, so Lima time = UTC - 5.

17:00 UTC → Lima: 17:00 - 5 = **12:00 noon**.

Both Eastern (post-fallback, EST = UTC-5) and Lima (PET = UTC-5) are the same offset, so the deadline is the same clock time in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is UTC-12. Tokyo is JST = UTC+9.

The difference between Tokyo and AoE is 9 - (-12) = +21 hours.

"December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" = January 1, 2027, 00:00 AoE (UTC-12).

Converting to Tokyo time: January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC-12 = January 1, 2027, 00:00 + 21 hours = January 2, 2027, 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-02 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the New York time when it's 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026.

**Step 1: Determine Sydney's UTC offset on October 5, 2026.**

Sydney observes AEDT (Australian Eastern Daylight Time) during daylight saving time. In 2026, Australia's DST starts on the first Sunday of October. October 5, 2026 is a Monday — DST would have started on October 4, 2026 (first Sunday of October). So on October 5, Sydney is on AEDT = UTC+11.

**Step 2: Convert Sydney time to UTC.**

5:00 PM Sydney AEDT (UTC+11) on October 5, 2026:
UTC = 17:00 - 11:00 = 06:00 UTC on October 5, 2026.

**Step 3: Determine New York's UTC offset on October 5, 2026.**

In the US, DST ends on the first Sunday of November. So on October 5, 2026, New York is still on EDT = UTC-4.

**Step 4: Convert UTC to New York time.**

New York = 06:00 UTC - 4 hours = 02:00 on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
